messages:
elaine: Quick Q during the all-hands — can we clarify how credits, quotas, and rate limits behave when a customer upgrades/downgrades packages? Do in-flight grace periods carry over? :thinking:

matt: Short answer: grace windows are tied to the billing bucket on the account at the time we apply them. But there are edge cases — happy to explain the flow.

sophia: To expand: when you upgrade, the new package's quotas apply immediately for new allocations. Any active "grace" tokens that were granted (e.g., promotional credits or temporary overage grace) remain on the account until they expire or are consumed. They don't auto-increase to match the higher tier.

sam: Finance note: credits are a currency on the account. If you downgrade mid-cycle we don't claw back consumed credits; future monthly allocations will follow the new plan. Refunds for unused committed credits are handled case-by-case via support SLA.

riley: From an infra/rate-limit perspective: there are two separate controls — per-token quota (billing/credits) and rate limiting (requests/second). Rate limit windows are enforced by the routing layer. We don't automatically widen rate limits on upgrade until the provisioning pipeline completes (usually < 5 minutes).

elaine: @matt @sophia ok, couple follow-ups: 1) If a customer has a "grace period" due to an outage (we applied a temporary buffer), and they switch to Dedicated during that buffer, does the buffer still apply? 2) When we say "quota fallthrough" to cheaper model variants as a fallback, does that still consume the same credits or a different bucket?

matt: 1) Yes — outage buffers are tagged to the account id and persist across plan changes until the buffer expiry time. We track buffers as metadata on the billing bucket. 2) Fallthrough: if we route to a cheaper model variant, the billing uses the billed model id at request time. So credits consumed reflect the variant used. We surface this in traces and billing breakdowns.

andre: Adding customer-safety perspective: we try to avoid surprising customers. When fallthrough changes the unit price by >10% we emit an event and a billing note they can opt into via account settings.

elaine: Nice. Another angle: streaming tokens — if you stream partial responses and then get rate-limited mid-stream, how are tokens billed?

riley: Good one. Tokens are metered at commit points (currently at chunk flush / message end). If a stream is cut by rate limiting, tokens up to the last confirmed flush are billed. We log X-Stream-Bytes and X-RateLimit-Remaining in the response headers. Example headers:

```
X-RateLimit-Limit: 120
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 32
X-Stream-Flushed-Tokens: 2460
```

sam: For clarity: billed tokens from a partial stream are deducted from credits — there's no automatic rollback unless we applied a customer credit adjustment.

elaine: How should customers request temporary quota increases for launches? Is there a self-serve flow or do they need support?

sophia: We're rolling out a self-serve temporary quota request UI in the Console next month. Until then: use the support form with the "quota-increase" tag and include expected RPS and duration. Recommended payload (for support API):

```
POST /v1/admin/quota-requests
{
  "account_id": "acct_ABC",
  "reason": "product launch",
  "start_ts": "2026-04-01T00:00:00Z",
  "end_ts": "2026-04-07T00:00:00Z",
  "tokens_per_min": 500000,
  "contact": "eng@example.com"
}
```

matt: Ops SLA: if you submit with the standard form and include telemetry (seq distribution, p95 latency) we can usually approve within 24 hours for launches. For multi-region bursts allow 48 hours.

elaine: Great. One last governance question — internal health checks and monitoring pings: do those count against quotas? Some customers worried their internal pings will blow through credits.

riley: Internal pings from our managed telemetry (e.g., heartbeat probes we run for Dedicated) are excluded if they originate from our health-check IP ranges and use the agent API key. Customer-originated pings (from their apps) do count. We recommend using lower-cost monitoring endpoints where possible.

andre: Also, if a large customer runs synthetic load tests, we encourage them to request a testing bucket — these are isolated and don't touch production credits. Contact support and we'll provision.

elaine: Thanks all — any roadmap timelines we should call out publicly?

sophia: Timeline recap: self-serve temporary quota UI in Console: mid-May. Per-route SLO billing visibility (route-level token breakdown) beta: June. Automated fallthrough alerts for >10% price delta: rolling in April. We'll publish a short doc and toolbar banners before changes go live.

matt: We'll follow up in the all-hands notes with links and a short FAQ. If you want to run through specific customer scenarios, ping me or @sophia and we'll schedule a customer ops sync. :thumbsup:

billing-bot: Note: Created internal task #BILL-534 to add explanatory copy to Console and to set up event triggers for fallthrough alerts.

elaine: Perfect — thanks everyone. I'll save the thread and include the FAQ link in the follow-up email.

sam: Thanks! Also logging a small follow-up to finance for refund policy edge cases.

andre: I'll take the support checklist item and make a playbook for handling downgrade-refund requests.

matt: Appreciate it. End of thread.
